At larger beta the exact response identity remains, while its available summable covariance estimate is open.

wilson_transfer.definition: For finite periodic spatial cubic Gamma with side≥3, X=SU(N)^{E_s}, A_beta(U)=exp[-(beta/2) sum_{p in P_s}(1-w(U_p))], k_beta(U,V)=product_{e in E_s} exp[beta w(U_e V_e^{-1})], K_beta(U,V)=integral dh k_beta(U,h.V), and T_beta=A_beta K_beta A_beta. P is full spatial gauge Haar projection; T=A k P A on invariant states. The open-time slab carries A at both ends, A^2 in the interior, and k between adjacent slices; temporal gauge fixing retains spatial holonomies and the terminal half-factor.

local_ground_state_response.definition: For bottom boundary edge e, changing U_e to U'_e inserts only H_e(V)=beta[w(U'_e V_e^dagger)-w(U_e V_e^dagger)] on first-layer copy (e,1), with |H_e|≤2beta and full oscillation ≤4beta. For distinct e,f, interpolate sH_e+tH_f in the normalized actual slab rho_(s,t), retaining every spatial plaquette, slab depth, and top boundary factor. The mixed finite difference of log R_n=log(psi_n/A(U_0)) is the integral over s,t in [0,1]^2 of Cov_{rho_(s,t)}(H_e,H_f). Perron limiting n gives the ground-state log-ratio identity.

soft_kernel_and_path_geometry.definition: At one S4' step lambda=kappa/g_i^2>0; M_c(U)=(4!L^4)^-1 sum_(sigma,y) T_y^sigma(U), and normalized SU(2) kernel k_lambda(V_c;M_c)=exp[lambda w(V_c^{-1}M_c)]/Z(lambda,M_c). The exact path words T_y^sigma are supplied by referenced PROOF.md Decision 4/D4-norm and are not redefined in this source note. For M=rW, Z(z)=2I_1(z)/z and E[V_c|U]=f_lambda(r)M_c, f=b(lambda r)/r, b=I_2/I_1, continuous at r=0. Distinct coarse links are conditionally independent; fine path footprints may overlap, retaining fine-field dependence in Cov_mu_beta(B_C,B_D).

exact_definitions_and_geometry.block_geometry_caveat: For a block B of b spatial links, p_B counts spatial plaquettes touching B. The ground-state finite-energy ratio is D_B=2beta(p_B+b), but it has no distance tail. The source suggests fixed-physical-radius block comparison, with all-sector boundary data, but gives no block-posterior response formula or estimate beyond the single-link mixed response and the strong-coupling Dobrushin comparison.

existing_response_and_mixing_results.content: The two source derivatives of normalized slab log partition are the covariance of H_e,H_f, integrated over both interpolation parameters. This exactly characterizes boundary response, with no estimate implied at arbitrary beta.

For positive finite product Gibbs density and symmetric influence majorant C with row q<1, D=(I-C)^-1 gives |Cov(f,g)|≤(1/4) sum_ij delta_i f D_ij delta_j g. For the actual half-slab, C^+_{(e,t),(f,s)}=beta[m_ef 1_{t=s}+1_{e=f}1_{|t-s|=1}], row 14beta. Thus for beta<1/14 the ground-state mixed response is bounded by 4 beta^2 D^+_{(e,1),(f,1)} after the direct local plaquette term is accounted for. The resolvent decays in graph distance uniformly in slab depth, spatial volume, and bottom boundary field.

existing_response_and_mixing_results.statement: Actual physical Doob posterior and contraction
existing_response_and_mixing_results.content: The output conditional keeps both A(V) and psi(V), plus the input-link kernel factor. Its off-diagonal output influence is C^step_ef=beta m_ef+beta^2 D^+_{(e,1),(f,1)}; row Q(beta)=12beta+beta^2/(1-14beta). An input-link perturbation has TV defect ≤beta at the same output edge, and comparison gives summed link oscillation contraction r=beta/[1-Q(beta)]. For 0<beta≤1/32, r≤18/359. This is a one-link influence norm for the actual posterior, but only in the small-beta endpoint.

existing_response_and_mixing_results.statement: All-beta local posterior tilt / finite energy
existing_response_and_mixing_results.content: For changing B of b links, Perron equation and touched plaquettes give log oscillation bound for pi=psi^2 conditional density: 2beta p_B+4beta b. Volume-independent for fixed finite B, but no decay with distance; block size comparable to fixed physical radius has b growing as (ell/a)^3.

existing_response_and_mixing_results.statement: Normalized soft-kernel source cumulants and total covariance
existing_response_and_mixing_results.content: For disjoint coarse edge sets, Cov_{mu_beta K_lambda}(W_C,W_D)=Cov_{mu_beta}(B_C,B_D); plaquette covariance has order-eight coefficient 4^-8 Cov_mu_beta(X_P,X_Q), with uniform bounded-coefficient remainder but no separation decay. For all fine local sources, integral dV W_lambda(V;J)=Z_beta(J); at lambda=0, W_0(V;J)=Z_beta(J), so its field-independent source-dependent log term differentiates to the original fine covariance. At lambda>0, Cov_mu(F,G)=Cov_nu(E[F|V],E[G|V])+E_nu Cov(F,G|V); both coarse covariance and conditional covariance need control. No full fine-to-coarse return/source map with decaying tails is supplied.

The unresolved quantity is the uniform, spatially summable Cov_{rho_(s,t;Gamma,n,U)}(H_e,H_f) for the actual Wilson half-slab at every depth, volume, bottom field, and interpolation; a physically sufficient block version must retain all boundary sectors. The construction note separately names a local block comparison for the actual ground-state kernel via exterior-data dependence of the Perron ratio, and a fixed-physical-scale two-source coefficient including source-only and conditional covariance terms.
